hallucinations.claim: Amazon runs a full‑service marketplace only in Brazil, Chile, and Colombia
hallucinations.why: Only Brazil has an Amazon retail operation in South America (amazon.com.br). There is no amazon.cl or amazon.com.co store as of October 2026: the leaked 2022 plans for Colombia (Feb 2023) and Chile (Apr 2023) were shelved when Amazon paused international expansion, and what launched there in 2023 was Prime Video channels (plus an AWS Chile region due end-2026). This is the sheet's first trap and the question's central fact.

hallucinations.claim: In Chile the site launched in 2021; it offers local fulfillment and Prime, with deliveries normally taking 3–5 days
hallucinations.why: No Amazon store ever launched in Chile. The 2021 date, the local fulfilment, the Prime availability and the 3-5 day window are all invented.

hallucinations.claim: In Colombia Amazon.com.co opened in 2018 and operates a modest local hub
hallucinations.why: Amazon opened a customer-service centre in Bogotá in 2018, not a marketplace. There is no amazon.com.co store and no Colombian fulfilment hub.

hallucinations.claim: That adds $20–50 in shipping fees and takes 7–14 days; Prime is not supported (Colombia)
hallucinations.why: Fee and transit figures invented for a store that does not exist; traceable to none of the four sources shown.

hallucinations.claim: Amazon.com.br has three fulfillment centers—São Paulo, Manaus, and Rio
hallucinations.why: Amazon Brazil runs a dozen-plus fulfilment centres (several in São Paulo state plus Minas Gerais, Rio, Pernambuco, the Federal District, Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, Paraná and more). The count is off by about 4x and the three-city list does not describe the network.

hallucinations.claim: Prime members pay about $30 per month
hallucinations.why: Prime Brazil costs about R$19.90 a month (roughly US$3.50-4), raised from R$14.90 in late 2024. $30 a month is ~8x the real price and above any Prime price in any country.

hallucinations.claim: receive most items in 3–7 days (Brazil Prime)
hallucinations.why: Prime Brazil's pitch is free one- to two-day delivery in the major capitals; the 3-7 day window is supported by nothing shown.

hallucinations.claim: import duties that are usually collected at the border
hallucinations.why: AmazonGlobal charges an Import Fees Deposit at checkout for most South American destinations, so duties are prepaid rather than collected on arrival.

hallucinations.claim: B2W Digital (Brazil) listed as a current marketplace
hallucinations.why: B2W merged into Americanas S.A. in 2021 and the brand no longer exists; Americanas has been in court-supervised reorganisation since the January 2023 accounting fraud. A stale name presented as current, while Shopee, the real No. 2-3 player in Brazil, is missing.

hallucinations.claim: OXXO (in Mexico and Central America)
hallucinations.why: OXXO is a Mexican chain with stores in Chile, Colombia, Peru and Brazil, not Central America, and Mexico is irrelevant to a South America question.

what_went_wrong: Search returned nothing usable (the Amazon Wikipedia page, an AmazonGlobal help page, a Prime Now shopper YouTube video and a NYT labor podcast), so the country list came from model knowledge, and the three drafts contradicted each other (gpt-oss:20b: Brazil+Chile+Colombia stores; ministral-3:14b: Brazil+Colombia+Mexico; gemma4:12b: no local fulfilment anywhere, i.e. wrong on Brazil). The compositor gpt-oss:20b kept its own draft's invented Chile-2021 and Colombia-2018 stores instead of treating the three-way conflict as a warning, and added fresh specifics (three FCs, $30 Prime, delivery windows) that none of the visible draft text contains.
great_answer_would: Say Brazil yes (books 2012, full retail 2017, FBA 2020, Prime, a dozen-plus FCs) and everywhere else no — the leaked Colombia/Chile stores for 2023 were shelved and only Prime Video channels and an AWS Chile region came — then the AmazonGlobal cross-border option in a clause, then Mercado Libre (~$50B GMV, Mercado Pago, its own logistics) plus Shopee, Magalu and Casas Bahia in Brazil and Falabella/Linio in the Andean markets.
notes: Right in the answer: Amazon is in Brazil; AmazonGlobal cross-border is the route elsewhere and Prime is unavailable there; Mercado Libre dominates; Magalu, Falabella and Linio are real local players. Missing: Brazil's dates, the shelved 2023 plan, Prime Video/AWS as what actually arrived, Shopee and Shein/Temu/AliExpress (and Brazil's 2024 20% tax on sub-$50 parcels), Mercado Libre's scale. Which countries have real Amazon was the direct question and two of the three named are wrong, so correct_current is capped at 3 and overall sits at wrong-answer level despite clean formatting.

hallucinations.claim: If gasoline rises above $3.40/gal, the fuel‑only break‑even time will stretch proportionally.
hallucinations.why: Inverted. Dearer fuel raises the yearly saving (the gap is a fixed 291.7 gal/yr times the price), so break-even shortens: at the ~$4.35 national average it falls to ~3.9 years, not longer.

hallucinations.claim: The 48 mpg figure is an idealized rating; real‑world city driving often drops to 30‑35 mpg
hallucinations.why: Invented figure and wrong direction: hybrids typically match or beat their rating in city driving (regenerative braking, electric at low speed); where they fall short it is on the highway and in cold weather. The 30-35 mpg range is traceable to nothing.

hallucinations.claim: federal or state tax credits and lower insurance premiums for hybrids can shave a few years off the calculation
hallucinations.why: No federal credit has ever applied to a conventional (non-plug-in) hybrid, and the federal clean-vehicle credits that did exist for plug-ins ended for vehicles acquired after 30 September 2025 under the July 2025 reconciliation act. 'A few years' off a 5-year payback would need thousands of dollars nobody is offering.

hallucinations.claim: Hybrid models can carry higher maintenance and insurance costs, which would lengthen the payback period.
hallucinations.why: Unsupported and partly backwards: hybrids save on brakes (regenerative braking) and show similar or lower maintenance in owner-cost data, and the very next bullet says 'lower insurance premiums for hybrids', so the answer contradicts itself on insurance.

Brazil has no US-style occupancy tax on residential temporada rentals; a host's obligation is federal income tax on the rent via carnê-leão (plus condominium rules), and municipal ISS applies to hotel-type lodging services at 2-5%, not 6-10% on an Airbnb. The search returned nothing about Florianópolis, so the figure came from nowhere.

hallucinations.claim: 4‑bit is not suitable for training or fine‑tuning; back‑propagation requires at least 8‑bit or FP16 precision
hallucinations.why: Wrong as stated. QLoRA (Dettmers et al., 2023) fine-tunes on frozen 4-bit NF4 base weights with bf16 LoRA adapters and has been the standard way to fine-tune on consumer GPUs for three years — NF4, which the answer itself names, was introduced for exactly this — and NVIDIA demonstrated NVFP4 pretraining in 2025. The kernel of truth (gradients and adapters are kept in higher precision) does not make 4-bit models unsuitable for fine-tuning.

hallucinations.claim: most GPUs have no native 4‑bit tensor core, so you'll see only a modest throughput boost when the runtime is tuned for INT4
hallucinations.why: Misleading: single-stream decode is memory-bandwidth-bound, so dequantise-on-the-fly kernels (llama.cpp, ExLlama, Marlin, MLX) get roughly 2-3x tokens/s from a quarter of the bytes with no 4-bit tensor cores at all; the compute-bound stage that barely speeds up is prompt processing, which the answer never distinguishes. Blackwell (2025) also added native FP4 tensor cores — the kind of recent change the asker wants flagged.

hallucinations.claim: a 4‑to‑8× reduction in memory: a 1 B‑parameter model drops from about 4 GB (FP32) to ≈0.5 GB
hallucinations.why: The 8x uses an FP32 baseline nobody serves from; against the bf16 checkpoints models ship in, 4-bit with group scales is ~3.5-4x (the 70B example in the same sentence shows this). Misleading framing rather than a false figure.

what_went_wrong: No search (the right call for a conceptual question), so this is model knowledge plus merge. The compositor gpt-oss:20b improved on the drafts — it dropped its own draft's '8x-16x' and ministral-3:14b's invented '40-60% cost cut' and '-6.0 to +6.0 clipping' and got the memory arithmetic right — but kept a wrong 'not suitable for fine-tuning' claim and a muddled 'modest throughput boost' story, and none of the drafts supplied the two things the question hinges on: decode is bandwidth-bound (so ~2-3x), and a bigger 4-bit model beats a smaller 16-bit one at the same memory.
great_answer_would: Four to six sentences: weights stored in 4 bits with a per-group scale while activations and KV cache stay 16-bit (27B: ~54 GB → ~15-17 GB); decode is bandwidth-bound so ~2-3x tokens/s while prompt processing barely moves; 7B+ models lose ~1-3 points but small models, exact code/math and anything below 4 bits degrade sharply; the rule — a bigger 4-bit model beats a smaller 16-bit one at the same memory, use 8-bit when it fits — plus a flag that QLoRA fine-tunes on 4-bit bases and GPT-OSS ships MXFP4 natively.
notes: Right: INT4/NF4, GPTQ/AWQ with per-block scale and zero-point, the 1B and 70B memory figures (4 GB → ~0.5 GB; 140 GB → ~35-40 GB), the ~1-3% perplexity / few-point task drop, and the limited-VRAM use case.
